chapters.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: Represent chemical reactions and identify common reaction types.
chapters.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

lessons.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
lessons.summary: Balance equations using conservation of atoms.

content_blocks.text: A chemical equation is balanced when each element has the same number of atoms on both sides. Change coefficients, never subscripts.
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side.
Balancing follows the law of conservation of mass.

concepts.title: Conservation of mass
concepts.explanation: Atoms are rearranged in a reaction; they are not created or destroyed.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

lessons.title: Types of Chemical Reactions
lessons.summary: Identify combination, decomposition, displacement and double-displacement reactions.

content_blocks.text: Many reactions follow one of four patterns: combination (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), displacement (A + BC → AC + B) and double displacement (AB + CD → AD + CB).
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu is a displacement reaction; 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ is a decomposition reaction.
Look at which atoms pair up — the pattern decides the reaction type.

concepts.title: Reaction types
concepts.explanation: Combination, decomposition, displacement and double displacement patterns.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: Which coefficient balances H₂ + O₂ → H₂O?
questions.explanation: Two water molecules require two hydrogen molecules and one oxygen molecule.

questions.prompt: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ is which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: A single compound breaks down into two or more products.

chapters.title: Life Processes
chapters.summary: Explain nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion in living organisms.
chapters.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 6, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

lessons.title: Photosynthesis: Making Food
lessons.summary: Trace how green plants make glucose using light energy.
learning_objectives: State the word equation for photosynthesis
Explain the role of chlorophyll and stomata

content_blocks.text: Green plants use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. Chlorophyll captures the light energy.
Leaves are the main photosynthetic organs; stomata enable gas exchange.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis
concepts.explanation: The process by which green plants synthesise food using light energy.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 6, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: Why is chlorophyll essential for photosynthesis?
questions.answer: It absorbs light energy used to drive photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll transfers captured light energy into the chemical process.

lessons.title: Respiration: Breaking Down Food for Energy
lessons.summary: Contrast aerobic and anaerobic respiration and locate the respiratory organs.
learning_objectives: Trace gas exchange in plants and animals

content_blocks.text: Respiration releases energy from glucose. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to yield CO₂, water and more ATP; anaerobic respiration runs without oxygen and produces ethanol or lactic acid with less ATP.
Oxygen availability decides whether respiration is aerobic or anaerobic.

concepts.title: Respiration
concepts.explanation: The process of releasing energy from glucose inside living cells.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Science Class X, Chapter 6, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy than aerobic respiration?
questions.answer: Glucose is incompletely oxidised in anaerobic respiration, so less energy is extracted.
questions.explanation: Complete oxidation of glucose captures much more chemical energy as ATP.
